# PLAN — iteration 3

## Current state assessment

Iteration 1 established a verified best at 3 LUTs and 4 FFs, with setup and hold passing; iteration 2 had the same resource counts and was rejected for no strict objective gain. The current seed already uses a 3-bit run counter and registered `clean`, so repeating that structure is unlikely to improve the `minimize_luts` objective.

## Hypothesis

Replacing the binary increment and terminal-count logic with a 3-bit maximal-length LFSR sequence may reduce the counter’s next-state logic enough to lower routed LUT use below 3 while retaining 4 FFs and timing closure.

## Instruction for generator

Keep `clean_reg` registered and preserve synchronous active-high reset and the `// @latency 0` annotation. Replace `run_count`’s binary increment with a 3-bit LFSR state that starts on the first sample differing from `clean_reg`, advances on each consecutive differing sample, and updates `clean_reg` on exactly the eighth such sample; reset the run state whenever `noisy == clean_reg`. Preserve the exact sample count and output behavior, and retain this candidate only if all verification gates pass and routed LUT use is strictly below the incumbent’s 3 LUTs.
